{d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a : Fin (q + 1) => ω a i)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i =>
    (((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ)) * Real.pi) / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      ((Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) → (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) → ℝ) := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun a => row i ω a) (fun a => row i ω a))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  (∀ i : Fin d, Measurable (Y i)) ∧ iIndepFun Y μ

literal_definition_excerpts.literal_source:
namespace OuterMeasure

/-- `OuterMeasure.pi m` is the finite product of the outer measures `{m i | i : ι}`.
  It is defined to be the maximal outer measure `n` with the property that
  `n (pi univ s) ≤ ∏ i, m i (s i)`, where `pi univ s` is the product of the sets
  `{s i | i : ι}`. -/
protected def pi (m : ∀ i, OuterMeasure (α i)) : OuterMeasure (∀ i, α i) :=
  boundedBy (piPremeasure m)

/-- `Measure.pi μ` is the finite product of the measures `{μ i | i : ι}`.
  It is defined to be measure corresponding to `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.pi`. -/
protected irreducible_def pi : Measure (∀ i, α i) :=
  toMeasure (OuterMeasure.pi fun i => (μ i).toOuterMeasure) (pi_caratheodory μ)

/-- A family of sets of sets `π : ι → Set (Set Ω)` is independent with respect to a measure `μ` if
for any finite set of indices `s = {i_1, ..., i_n}`, for any sets
`f i_1 ∈ π i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ π i_n`, then `μ (⋂ i in s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, μ (f i) `.
It will be used for families of π-systems. -/
def iIndepSets {_mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (π : ι → Set (Set Ω)) (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) : Prop :=
  Kernel.iIndepSets π (Kernel.const Unit μ) (Measure.dirac () : Measure Unit)

/-- Two sets of sets `s₁, s₂` are independent with respect to a measure `μ` if for any sets

Kernel.IndepSets s1 s2 (Kernel.const Unit μ) (Measure.dirac () : Measure Unit)

/-- A family of measurable space structures (i.e. of σ-algebras) is independent with respect to a
measure `μ` (typically defined on a finer σ-algebra) if the family of sets of measurable sets they
define is independent. `m : ι → MeasurableSpace Ω` is independent with respect to measure `μ` if
for any finite set of indices `s = {i_1, ..., i_n}`, for any sets
`f i_1 ∈ m i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ m i_n`, then `μ (⋂ i in s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, μ (f i)`. -/
def iIndep (m : ι → MeasurableSpace Ω) {_mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) :
    Prop :=
  Kernel.iIndep m (Kernel.const Unit μ) (Measure.dirac () : Measure Unit)

/-- A family of functions defined on the same space `Ω` and taking values in possibly different
spaces, each with a measurable space structure, is independent if the family of measurable space
structures they generate on `Ω` is independent. For a function `g` with codomain having measurable
space structure `m`, the generated measurable space structure is `MeasurableSpace.comap g m`. -/
def iIndepFun {_mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {β : ι → Type*} [m : ∀ x : ι, MeasurableSpace (β x)]
    (f : ∀ x : ι, Ω → β x) (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) : Prop :=
  Kernel.iIndepFun f (Kernel.const Unit μ) (Measure.dirac () : Measure Unit)

definition_kinds.meaning: d-dimensional standard Gaussian columns on their finite product; coordinate row in Euclidean(q+1)-space, source indices a.val+1 and i.val+1. No Gaussian law on an Omega function norm is asserted.

Independence of the inverse-image sigma-algebras, hence factorization for every finite intersection of measurable row events. The implementation expands through Kernel.iIndepFun/iIndep/iIndepSets and a constant kernel on Unit under dirac(). It is not pairwise independence only, does not assert injectivity or identical distribution, and by itself does not assert measurability of arbitrary maps.
L=2(q+1)+3log(1000d), theta_i=(i.val+1-1/2)pi/d, feature0=1 and featurek=sqrt2cos(k theta_i). No Gram or norm bound is an input.

A real matrix is definitionally a function of two finite paired indices. The explicit function carrier exposes its canonical product measurable structure without an opaque local type alias or additional typeclass hypothesis. The Gaussian coordinate precedes the feature coordinate in both paired indices. No matrix operator-norm assertion is made by this independence statement.

The closed cutoff selects inverse-d times the Kronecker product of actual Gaussian-row and deterministic-feature outer products; outside the event it is zero, exactly the source indicator. This is not an existence/default definition.

All actual Y maps are measurable AND the entire family is iIndepFun under that same mu. Neither measurability nor independence is a new input certificate. The matrices need not be identically distributed because features vary with i.
